summary_paragraph: The patient, a man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, epilepsy, and cardiomyopathy, was admitted with fever, confusion, and hypotension during dialysis. He was diagnosed with bacterial pneumonia superimposed on recent influenza, leading to severe sepsis and toxic metabolic encephalopathy. Imaging confirmed right lower lobe pneumonia, and an echocardiogram revealed newly reduced ejection fraction of 15% and severe mitral regurgitation, though stress testing showed no new coronary blockages. He was treated with intravenous antibiotics, including vancomycin and piperacillin-tazobactam, completed a course of dialysis, and had his heart and seizure medications adjusted. His infection resolved, mental status improved, and he was discharged to an extended care facility with plans for cardiology follow-up, dental evaluation, and monitoring of a thyroid nodule and lung nodule.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic (congestive) heart failure
Epilepsy, unspecified, not intractable, without status epilepticus
Hemiplegia and hemiparesis following cerebral infarction affecting right dominant side
